text:
Alex R: Heads-up - prod-rtpool spiked OOMs across 4 hosts starting 12:13 UTC. multiple cudaMalloc OOMs, same batch window. infra-bot created incident 9872.

infra-bot: Incident 9872 created for prod-rtpool:oom-spike - paging oncall.

Maria G: I'm seeing allocator churn right before the OOMs in the flamegraphs. workspace alloc/free rate goes through the roof at batch boundary. attaching summary in the thread.

Samir: uploaded quick profile (flame + allocation timeline). key pattern: repeated allocate->free->allocate of ~40-120MB buffers, thrashing the slab allocator when batch size spikes.

Kai L: quick mitigation we can flip: enable adaptive buffer cycler (temp fallback) so runtime retires hot buffers into a short LRU instead of immediate free/alloc. command (internal):
```
rwctl set feature adaptive_buffer_cycler=true --scope cluster --expires 15m
```

Jules: Also propose reducing kernel_A workspace cap on these hosts from 512 -> 320MB to avoid oversized reservations during bursts. small config patch: `kernel_selector.kernel_A.max_workspace_mb=320` applied to gpu-pool-a-{3,7,9,14}.

Tanvi P: request-shaping suggestion: cap user token windows for incoming requests hitting these hosts, queue micro-batches for 10ms to smooth bursts. runtime config: `queue.max_batch_ms=10` + `request.max_tokens=512`.

Alex R: Plan: 1) toggle adaptive_buffer_cycler on hotspot hosts, 2) trim kv cache TTL to free headroom, 3) reduce kernel_A workspace cap, 4) enable route-level rate limiter for high-TPS keys. roll will be canary then 4-host roll.

Samir: I trimmed kv default TTL from 2400 -> 1800s on the 4 hosts to reclaim ~1GB each. command I used: `rwctl set config kv.default_ttl_sec=1800 --hosts gpu-pool-a-3,gpu-pool-a-7,gpu-pool-a-9,gpu-pool-a-14`.

Maria G: log excerpt from host gpu-pool-a-9 around 12:13: `E runtime allocator: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 67108864) - free list len=3; last_free=12s ago` then immediate recovery attempts. looks like reuse path returned false.

Kai L: there's a suspected race in reuse tag invalidation when buffers are concurrently returned to the global pool. aggressive reuse policy helps but could mask bug. temporary setting: `allocator.reuse_policy=aggressive` (expires 15m). risk: latent stale pointer if bug exists, but acceptable for short mitigation window.

Jules: I'm on-call to monitor. I'll prepare rollback patch to set adaptive_buffer_cycler=false and restore default kernel_workspace cap if we see latency regressions.

Tanvi P: monitoring thresholds to watch (please add alerts if not present): `oom.count >= 1 on host` (critical), `allocator.churn_ms > 200` (warn), `kv.evictions > 50m` (warn), `batch.latency_p50 > 400ms` (warn).

Alex R: I've applied the toggles to the 4 hosts, started canary at 12:20 UTC. infra-bot shows deploy job succeeded.

infra-bot: deploy job finished: feature adaptive_buffer_cycler=true applied to gpu-pool-a-3,gpu-pool-a-7,gpu-pool-a-9,gpu-pool-a-14.

Alex R: Update - after 12 minutes OOM count on those hosts dropped to 0. batch latency increased ~5-12ms p50 but stable; allocator churn metric down ~60%. will keep canary for 15m then promote if no regressions.

Samir: observed secondary effect: kv-hit rate dropped slightly due to TTL trim, but net memory reclaimed >1.1GB/host. fine tradeoff for short windows.

Maria G: recording root-cause hypothesis: allocator reuse path didn't reclaim fast enough under bursty allocate/free cycles; combined with large per-kernel workspace reservation, that pushed live usage above device capacity. follow-ups: 1) add a small adaptive backoff in alloc path, 2) add metrics for reuse_fail_count, 3) add unit test for concurrent return path.

Jules: Ack. I'll open a follow-up ticket for allocator unit tests and kernel workspace audit.

Alex R: TL;DR: temporary mitigations applied (adaptive cycler + ttl trim + workspace cap + request shaping). OOMs stopped on canary. Keeping monitoring and will promote in 15m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Tanvi P: I'll keep watch on user-facing error rate and latency. ping me if anything spikes above the thresholds.

Jules: on-call ready to rollback. :eyes:

infra-bot: incident 9872: state=investigating -> mitigated (adaptive buffer cycler applied).

Alex R: Final update 12:50 UTC - canary promoted to full pool; OOMs remain 0, latency +7ms p50 but within SLO. closing incident in 30m unless new alerts.
